basis: Intellectual disability, cataracts and hypogonadism define syndrome; hip osteonecrosis and scoliosis each reported in 2/2 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Airway dysfunction defines disease; allergen or infection triggers do not establish an immune or infectious disease mechanism.
Inherited adenoma originates in the parathyroid endocrine gland; common extra-glandular damage is not established.
Inherited frontal lobe epilepsy is a brain disorder; behavioral manifestations do not establish another organ axis.
Aneurysmal disease directly affects the thoracic aortic wall.
Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction and neurodevelopmental impairment define disease; scoliosis in 150/180 and strabismus in 30-79% support additional axes.
ACTA1-related skeletal myopathy; respiratory dysfunction reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage; cardiac involvement is rare.
Microcephaly, brain malformations, developmental disability and primordial dwarfism define syndrome; joint contractures are frequent; renal and hearing defects are occasional.
Segmental lower motor neuron degeneration causes upper-limb weakness and denervation; no independent primary muscle disease.
Ischial hypoplasia or aplasia and vertebral malformations define this skeletal dysostosis.
Thumb ankylosis, brachydactyly and intellectual disability define syndrome; obesity alone does not establish direct endocrine damage.
Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia affects sweat glands and hair, with hypodontia in 7/7; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no extra-auditory disease is established.
Toxoplasma infection directly produces encephalitis or brain abscesses; underlying immunodeficiency is a separate condition.
Congenital hand-foot skeletal malformations include triphalangeal thumbs, polydactyly and syndactyly.
Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss is confined to the auditory axis.
Developmental disability and brainstem/cerebellar malformations define disease; ocular dysfunction in 2/2, with amblyopia and optic disc pallor in 1/2; small sample.
Pure anxiety disorder; muscle tension, fatigue and sleep symptoms do not establish organ damage.
Joubert syndrome ancestry establishes cerebellar/brainstem developmental disease; subtype evidence does not establish common renal or retinal damage.
Metabolic enzyme deficiency; cataracts in 3/4. Hepatic, cardiac and pancreatic abnormalities each in 1/4; neurologic frequency unspecified.
Benign mesothelial tumor confined to the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no axis.
Astrocytic tumor originates in the central nervous system; visual impairment depends on location and is not established in at least 30%.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease; myopia and strabismus in 1/1 reported patient support ocular involvement, with limited prevalence evidence.
Mixed colorectal polyposis defines disease; bleeding-related anemia is secondary and separately diagnosed; colorectal cancer is a separate consequence.
Pseudomonas infection directly causes pulmonary inflammation, alveolar hemorrhage and necrosis; associated neutropenia is an underlying condition.
